note: Attested evidence procedures. Every entry names an owner, an approval date and a review-due date. Status is derived from those dates at read time — an entry whose review is overdue degrades on its own, without anybody editing this file. Entries with an explicit status describe a control that is genuinely absent; they are not placeholders.

document-ai-governance-policy.summary: The AI governance policy names the accountable owner, the approval gate for model or corpus change, and the review cadence for this RAG service.

document-role-assignment.summary: A named accountable owner, service owner and reviewer are assigned for the assistant, with deputies recorded.

document-risk-register.summary: Retrieval, grounding, prompt-injection, tenant-isolation and vendor-dependency risks are registered with owners and treatment dates.

document-risk-treatment.summary: Each registered risk carries an accepted treatment, a residual-risk rating and a named approver.

document-human-oversight.summary: The escalation path from an unsatisfactory answer to a human responder is documented, including the shutdown switch and who may operate it.

document-incident-runbook.summary: The AI incident runbook covers grounding failure, guardrail bypass, corpus poisoning and provider outage, with notification timelines.

document-supplier-assessment.summary: OpenAI, MongoDB Atlas and Render are assessed for security posture, data handling and subprocessor disclosure.

document-vendor-contracts.summary: Contractual terms for the model provider and the vector store are registered, including data-use and retention commitments.

document-privacy-notice.summary: The published notice states what the assistant retains, what it sends to the model provider, and how to reach a human.

document-ai-transparency.summary: The web client discloses that responses are AI-generated and states the knowledge-base boundary.

document-system-card.summary: The system card records intended use, out-of-scope use, the retrieval design, the model and embedding versions, and known limitations.

document-change-policy.summary: Model, prompt and corpus changes require review, a passing test suite and a recorded approver before deployment.

document-feedback-process.summary: User-reported wrong answers are triaged, linked to the retrieved sources, and fed into corpus corrections.

document-training-program.summary: Operators of the assistant complete AI-literacy and escalation training with completion recorded.

document-evaluation-methodology.summary: The offline grounding and answer-quality evaluation methodology defines the question set, scoring rubric and acceptance thresholds.

artifact-bias-evaluation.summary: Answer quality was compared across industry and role segments of the question set, with variance recorded per segment.

artifact-threat-model.summary: The threat model covers the retrieval boundary, the model provider trust boundary, tenant isolation in the vector store, and indirect prompt injection through corpus content.

artifact-architecture-diagram.summary: The current architecture records every hop from the browser through the API, guardrails, vector store and model provider.

artifact-data-flow.summary: The data-flow record shows what leaves the service boundary, to which processor, and in which region.

artifact-output-sink-review.summary: Every sink that renders model output was reviewed; the web client inserts answers as text nodes and never as markup, and no output reaches a shell, query or template interpreter.

artifact-output-encoding.summary: Model output is treated as untrusted text: it is returned through a typed response model and rendered without HTML interpretation.

artifact-encryption-configuration.summary: Transport is TLS-terminated at the platform edge and the vector store enforces encryption at rest with provider-managed keys.

artifact-network-configuration.summary: Only the HTTPS service port is exposed; the vector store is reached outbound over TLS with an allow-listed source.

artifact-access-review.summary: Repository, platform and vector-store entitlements were reviewed against role, with least-privilege service accounts confirmed.

artifact-training-completion.summary: Completion records exist for every named operator of the assistant.

artifact-explainability-tests.summary: Answers are tested for citation fidelity: every claim in a grounded answer must map to a returned source chunk.

artifact-privacy-tests.summary: The response redaction path is unit-tested against synthetic identifiers, card numbers and contact details.

document-record-retention.summary: No retention schedule is configured or enforced for this deployment. Request traces expire on a fixed in-memory timer and stored corpus records have no defined disposal date.

document-disaster-recovery.summary: A recovery plan exists and names the rebuild path from source and re-ingestion, but it has never been exercised and no recovery-time objective has been measured.

document-backup-plan.summary: The vector store relies on the provider's managed snapshots. No independent restore of the corpus collection has been tested by this team.
